svg.title: Casual services invoice automation: a scheduled Lambda prepares an invoice and a Gmail draft, and a person sends it
svg.desc: Two CloudFormation stacks in one AWS account. The storage stack holds a private S3 bucket, a DynamoDB ledger and a Secrets Manager secret, and is kept if the stack is deleted. The runtime stack holds EventBridge Scheduler, a Lambda function, an SNS topic, CloudWatch alarms and an SQS dead-letter queue. On day three of the month the scheduler invokes the Lambda. It reads the configuration and PDF template from S3, reserves an invoice number in a DynamoDB transaction, saves the PDF and the complete email to S3, writes a creating marker, and creates one Gmail draft. SNS emails the operator, who reads the draft, sends it by hand and confirms the send from a command line tool. The ledger moves through reserved, prepared, creating, done and sent confirmed. If the outcome of the Gmail request is unknown, a retry looks for the operation ID in the existing drafts and adopts a single match; with none or several it stops for a person. Billable days come from working weekdays, regional public holidays and overrides, and five fields of the PDF template are replaced.
svg.text: A scheduled Lambda prepares the invoice and a Gmail draft - sending it stays a human action
Counter and month row are written
A failed number is never reused.
Emails me when a draft is ready
no send call in the code
I read the draft and send it myself
sent confirmation, entered by me from the command line
The stored phase decides what a repeated run is allowed to do.
A retry searches the drafts for the operation ID and adopts a single match.
None or several: the job stops and waits for me. No blind second request.
Billable days - how the amount is worked out
A year with no holiday calendar stops the run. It does not guess.
Nothing else on the page changes. Tests compare pixels outside the fields.
EventBridge Scheduler invokes the Lambda on day three of the month at 21:00 Melbourne time.
It reads the configuration and PDF template from S3, works out the charges and reserves the invoice number.
The PDF and the complete email are saved to S3, then a creating marker is written to the ledger.
With OAuth credentials from Secrets Manager it creates one Gmail draft. That request is not retried automatically.
The draft ID is recorded and SNS emails me that the invoice is ready.
I read the draft in Gmail and send it myself. The code has no send path.
I confirm the send from the command line. Only then does the ledger move to sent_confirmed.
